1	// Package natsmsg holds small JetStream message helpers shared by the
2	// hand-rolled pull consumers (permswebhook, repoops).
3	package natsmsg
4	
5	import (
6		"sync"
7		"time"
8	)
9	
10	// keepInProgressMaxTicks caps the total AckWait extension at ~5×AckWait
11	// (ticks fire at AckWait/3). The heartbeat exists so a long handler that IS
12	// making progress — a whole-installation teardown fan-out, a multi-GB
13	// data-plane purge — doesn't get redelivered into a concurrent duplicate;
14	// it must NOT remove the broker's liveness failsafe entirely, or a wedged
15	// handler (hung I/O with no deadline) would pin its delivery to the wedged
16	// replica forever. Past the cap the extension stops and AckWait expiry
17	// redelivers to a healthy replica sharing the durable.
18	const keepInProgressMaxTicks = 15
19	
20	// KeepInProgress calls inProgress at ackWait/3 until stop is called, resetting
21	// the broker's redelivery timer while a long handler runs. The extension is
22	// capped (keepInProgressMaxTicks) — see the constant for why.
23	//
24	// inProgress wraps the message's InProgress call — func() error { return
25	// msg.InProgress() }. The func() error callback keeps this helper decoupled
26	// from the jetstream package.
27	//
28	// A non-positive interval (zero ackWait on a hand-built consumer; New
29	// defaults it everywhere real) returns a no-op stop.
30	//
31	// stop is idempotent and blocks until the ticker goroutine has exited, so
32	// no InProgress can race a terminal disposition (Ack/Nak/Term) issued
33	// after it returns.
34	func KeepInProgress(inProgress func() error, ackWait time.Duration) (stop func()) {
35		interval := ackWait / 3
36		if interval <= 0 {
37			return func() {}
38		}
39		done := make(chan struct{})
40		finished := make(chan struct{})
41		go func() {
42			defer close(finished)
43			ticker := time.NewTicker(interval)
44			defer ticker.Stop()
45			for ticks := 0; ; {
46				select {
47				case <-done:
48					return
49				case <-ticker.C:
50					ticks++
51					if ticks > keepInProgressMaxTicks {
52						return
53					}
54					if err := inProgress(); err != nil {
55						// A delivery that can't be extended (no JetStream
56						// reply subject, or already terminally disposed)
57						// won't start succeeding on a later tick; stop
58						// instead of spinning. The real failure surfaces
59						// on the terminal Ack/Nak/Term.
60						return
61					}
62				}
63			}
64		}()
65		var once sync.Once
66		return func() {
67			once.Do(func() { close(done) })
68			<-finished
69		}
70	}

3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"strconv"
7		"time"

9		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go"
10		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"
11	)
12	
13	// dlqPublishTimeout bounds one dead-letter PublishMsg. The consume context has
14	// no deadline, and PublishMsg waits for the PubAck indefinitely; without a
15	// bound a NATS blip would hang the handler (and, since fetchBatch keeps a slot
16	// one-in-flight, stall the consumer) instead of failing the capture loudly.
17	const dlqPublishTimeout = 15 * time.Second
18	
19	// DLQ provenance headers added to the captured copy so a replay tool (or a
20	// human) can see why and from where a message was dead-lettered.
21	const (
22		DLQReasonHeader    = "Nats-Dlq-Reason"
23		DLQOriginHeader    = "Nats-Dlq-Origin-Subject"
24		DLQDeliveredHeader = "Nats-Dlq-Delivered"
25		DLQStreamSeqHeader = "Nats-Dlq-Stream-Seq"
26	)
27	
28	// DLQPublisher is the publish surface DeadLetter needs — satisfied by
29	// nats.JetStreamContext. Kept minimal so wiring can hand it the same
30	// JetStreamContext the per-cell publishers already hold, and tests can stub it.
31	type DLQPublisher interface {
32		PublishMsg(m *nats.Msg, opts ...nats.PubOpt) (*nats.PubAck, error)
33	}
34	
35	// SubjectToken sanitizes s into a single valid NATS subject token. NATS tokens
36	// cannot contain spaces, dots, or wildcards, so every character outside
37	// [a-z0-9_-] is replaced with '_' (and letters are lowercased). Use it to turn a
38	// human-readable dead-letter reason ("bad completion payload") into a subject
39	// token ("bad_completion_payload") — publishing to an unsanitized reason would
40	// fail, so the caller would never Ack the poison off the WorkQueue (COR-944).
41	func SubjectToken(s string) string {
42		// Iterate bytes, not runes: we only keep ASCII [a-z0-9_-] and map everything
43		// else (including every byte of a multi-byte rune) to '_', so a byte loop is
44		// both correct and free of a rune->byte narrowing conversion.
45		b := make([]byte, 0, len(s))
46		for i := range len(s) {
47			c := s[i]
48			switch {
49			case c >= 'a' && c <= 'z', c >= '0' && c <= '9', c == '_', c == '-':
50				b = append(b, c)
51			case c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z':
52				b = append(b, c-'A'+'a')
53			default:
54				b = append(b, '_')
55			}
56		}
57		if len(b) == 0 {
58			return "unknown"
59		}
60		return string(b)
61	}
62	
63	// DeadLetter republishes a poison message to dlqSubject, preserving its payload
64	// and headers and adding Nats-Dlq-* provenance (reason, origin subject,
65	// delivery count, stream sequence).
66	//
67	// It exists because repo_ops_v1 is a WorkQueue: a message leaves the stream
68	// only on a positive Ack. Term and MaxDeliver-exhaustion do NOT delete it — it
69	// lingers un-acked until StreamMaxAge, pinning the oldest-pending-age gauge
70	// (COR-944). So a consumer that can never process a message must DeadLetter it
71	// and then Ack the original.
72	//
73	// Returns an error if the republish fails; on error the caller MUST NOT Ack —
74	// Nak or leave the message so the poison is never dropped without a captured
75	// copy. Publishing is bounded by dlqPublishTimeout regardless of ctx's deadline.
76	func DeadLetter(ctx context.Context, pub DLQPublisher, dlqSubject string, msg jetstream.Msg, reason string) error {
77		hdr := nats.Header{}
78		for k, v := range msg.Headers() {
79			hdr[k] = append([]string(nil), v...)
80		}
81		hdr.Set(DLQReasonHeader, reason)
82		hdr.Set(DLQOriginHeader, msg.Subject())
83		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil && meta != nil {
84			hdr.Set(DLQDeliveredHeader, strconv.FormatUint(meta.NumDelivered, 10))
85			hdr.Set(DLQStreamSeqHeader, strconv.FormatUint(meta.Sequence.Stream, 10))
86		}
87	
88		out := &nats.Msg{Subject: dlqSubject, Data: msg.Data(), Header: hdr}
89	
90		pubCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, dlqPublishTimeout)
91		defer cancel()
92		if _, err := pub.PublishMsg(out, nats.Context(pubCtx)); err != nil {
93			return fmt.Errorf("dead-letter publish to %q: %w", dlqSubject, err)
94		}
95		return nil
96	}

2	// so a consumer span parents to the remote producer span — joining the ingest,

4	// mirror-pipeline/pkg/otelnats.

6	
7	import (
8		"context"

10		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go"
11		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel"

15	)

17	// HeaderCarrier adapts nats.Header to propagation.TextMapCarrier so the
18	// configured propagator can inject/extract traceparent and baggage.
19	type HeaderCarrier nats.Header
20	
21	func (c HeaderCarrier) Get(key string) string {
22		v := nats.Header(c).Values(key)
23		if len(v) == 0 {
24			return ""
25		}
26		return v[0]
27	}

29	func (c HeaderCarrier) Set(key, value string) {
30		nats.Header(c).Set(key, value)
31	}

34		keys := make([]string, 0, len(c))
35		for k := range c {
36			keys = append(keys, k)
37		}
38		return keys
39	}

42	// header map if absent. Call before publishing so the consumer can re-parent.
43	func Inject(ctx context.Context, msg *nats.Msg) {
44		if msg.Header == nil {
45			msg.Header = nats.Header{}
46		}
47		otel.GetTextMapPropagator().Inject(ctx, HeaderCarrier(msg.Header))
48	}

51	// before starting the consumer span so it parents to the remote producer.
52	func Extract(ctx context.Context, msg *nats.Msg) context.Context {

58	func ExtractHeader(ctx context.Context, h nats.Header) context.Context {
59		if h == nil {

2	// the service's decode-and-dispatch lifecycle consumers (repolifecycle,
3	// settingsconsumer, mirrorlifecycle). Each of those hand-rolled the same lifecycle:
4	// jetstream.New → CreateOrUpdateConsumer (durable, explicit ack, 30s ack-wait,
5	// bounded MaxDeliver, filter subject) → Consume → stop on context cancel; and the
6	// same per-message prologue: open a consumer span (re-parented across the NATS hop),
7	// decode the payload, and Term on a decode error.
8	//
9	// This package owns exactly that scaffold and nothing else. Each consumer keeps its
10	// OWN event type, business dispatch (op switch, seed/apply/push), metrics, and log
11	// lines — Start takes the consumer's message callback, and Process invokes the
12	// consumer's handle with the decoded event and the live span.
13	package jsconsumer

16		"context"
17		"fmt"
18		"log/slog"

33		// upsert, short enough that a stuck message redelivers promptly).
34		ackWait = 30 * time.Second
35		// defaultMaxDeliver caps redelivery before JetStream terms a message when the

41	// filter is given as either FilterSubject (single) or FilterSubjects (multi),
42	// mirroring jetstream.ConsumerConfig, so a migrated consumer preserves its existing
43	// on-server filter form exactly.
44	type Config struct {
45		Stream         string   // JetStream stream to bind (must already exist)
46		Durable        string   // durable consumer name, stable across restarts
47		FilterSubject  string   // set this OR FilterSubjects
48		FilterSubjects []string // set this OR FilterSubject

22	// labels the connection in the logs so a wedged drain can be attributed.

25	// phase; nats.go then runs an unconditional ~5s publish flush before closing,

27		return ctx.Err() != nil &&

29	}

31	// Drain drains nc and waits (bounded by timeout) for it to flush pending
32	// acks/publishes and reach CLOSED. nats.go's Conn.Drain is asynchronous — it
33	// starts the drain on a background goroutine and returns immediately — so a
34	// bare Drain in a shutdown cleanup would let the process exit before the flush
35	// completes. This subscribes to the connection's CLOSED status event, starts
36	// the drain, and blocks until the connection closes or timeout elapses. name
37	// labels the connection in the logs so a wedged drain can be attributed, and
38	// diagnostics are written to logger (defaulting to [slog.Default] when nil).
39	//
40	// timeout is the TOTAL time-to-CLOSED backstop, not the subscription-drain
41	// budget. The connect-time nats.DrainTimeout option caps only the
42	// subscription-drain phase; nats.go then runs an unconditional 5s publish flush
43	// before closing, so the true time-to-CLOSED is up to that flush longer than
44	// nats.DrainTimeout. timeout must exceed the connection's nats.DrainTimeout by
45	// at least the publish-flush budget or it will fire mid-drain and drop pending
46	// acks — [ShutdownGroup] sizes it automatically. timeout bounds how long we
47	// block; it is not a guarantee the drain finished. Once the consumer loops have
48	// joined (see [ShutdownGroup]) there is nothing left to drain, so on a reachable
49	// server this returns in milliseconds; the backstop only bites when the server

## Subpackages

The root package is deliberately nats.go-only. The consumer-side layers live in
subpackages so importing the root links none of their dependencies (`natsmsg`
and `jsconsumer` add the OpenTelemetry API; all three use `nats.go/jetstream`):

- **`natsmsg`** — small JetStream message helpers: W3C trace-context
  propagation over message headers (`Inject` / `ExtractHeader` /
  `StartConsumerSpan`, so publish → consume stitches into one trace) and
  `KeepInProgress`, an AckWait heartbeat for long handlers, capped so a wedged
  handler still redelivers. `natsmsg/natsmsgtest` ships `FakeMsg`, a scriptable
  `jetstream.Msg` for asserting a consumer's ack/nak/term disposition without a
  broker.
- **`jsconsumer`** — the durable JetStream pull-consumer scaffold:
  `Start` (create-or-update durable → consume → stop on context cancel) and
  `Process` (consumer span re-parented across the NATS hop → decode →
  Term-on-undecodable → dispatch to the handler, which owns the message's
  disposition). AckExplicit, bounded AckWait and MaxDeliver, shutdown-aware
  consume-error logging, optional `KeepInProgress` heartbeat.
- **`backoff`** — the redelivery policy for transiently-failed deliveries: a
  flat `NakWithDelay` envelope bounded by MaxDeliver, with opt-in
  Term-on-final-delivery so a work-queue message is removed cleanly instead of
  orphaning un-acked (COR-762).

## Blocker: Entire-Checkpoint trailers can't be produced in this session

AGENTS.md requires every commit to carry an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer added by a git hook. I made the first commit (`natsmsg`, `869e0ee` in go-nuts) and the trailer is missing. Digging in:

- The task-workspace clones have **no Entire git hooks** — `.git/hooks` isn't copied on clone, so `prepare-commit-msg`/`post-commit` from your main checkouts (e.g. `~/work/entire/go-nuts`) never made it here.
- Session tracking never started either: the repos' own `.claude/settings.json` files wire `entire hooks claude-code session-start` etc., but this session's cwd is the task root `~/work/tasks/go-nuts-extension`, which has **no `.claude` directory** — so no Entire session/checkpoint exists to stamp into a trailer even if the git hooks were present.
- I tried to remediate with `entire enable --agent claude-code --force` in go-nuts, but the permission system denied installing hooks (reasonable — it persists beyond the session).

Options: (a) you run `! cd go-nuts && entire enable --agent claude-code` (and the same in `entiredb`/`entire-api`) so the hooks exist — though the trailer may still need a tracked session; (b) you tell me to proceed without trailers for this task; (c) the task-workspace tooling gets fixed to install hooks at clone time. **I'll hold off on further commits/PRs until you weigh in** — happy to amend/redo `869e0ee` under whichever regime you pick.

## Work completed so far (all in the go-nuts working tree, tested + lint-clean)

All three packages from the issue's "grow go-nuts" section are built, with `mise run lint` at 0 issues and `go test -race ./...` green:

- **`natsmsg`** — the unified lift of entiredb's `internal/natsmsg` + entire-api's `otelnats`: `HeaderCarrier`, `Inject`/`Extract`/`ExtractHeader`, `StartConsumerSpan`, `ClampToInt64`, the capped `KeepInProgress` heartbeat, and `natsmsgtest.FakeMsg`. This commit also adds the OTel API dependency (the footprint decision the issue flags — root package stays nats.go-only, subpackages carry OTel/jetstream). Committed as `869e0ee` (sans trailer).
- **`jsconsumer`** — entire-api's scaffold with the two folds the issue asks for: consume errors are suppressed via `nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr` during shutdown (the COR-923 posture), and `Config.KeepInProgress` opts a consumer into the AckWait heartbeat around `handle`. Service-local deps became config: `Tracer`/`Logger` fields with sane defaults, `AckWait` now configurable (default 30s). Tests ported plus an embedded-JetStream end-to-end test for `Start`. Uncommitted.
- **`backoff`** — the COR-762 policy from `fanoutengine`, retargeted at `jetstream.Msg`: `Policy{NakDelay, MaxDeliver, TermOnExhaustion}.NakOrTerm()` returning `(Outcome, error)`, plus `IsFinalDelivery`/`NumDelivered` so callers can gate DLQ capture. Flat delay, Term-on-final-delivery opt-in. Uncommitted.
- README + root `doc.go` updated to describe the subpackages and the dependency posture. Uncommitted.

One design note: entiredb's `natsmsg` also has `DeadLetter`/`SubjectToken` (the COR-944 WorkQueue poison capture), which the issue's checkbox does *not* list for the lift — but the entiredb convergence bullet says to retire `internal/natsmsg` entirely, so those will need a go-nuts home (likely `natsmsg` too) when that migration happens. Flagging it now so it doesn't get lost.

Next after your call on the trailers: commit `jsconsumer`/`backoff`/docs, open the go-nuts PR, then start the entire-api convergence (fold `internal/jsconsumer` + `otelnats` back onto the module, adopt `nuts.Connect`/`Drain` — ~12 consumer files).

Command "attach" is deprecated, use 'entire session attach' instead
Attach an existing agent session that wasn't captured by hooks.

This creates a checkpoint from the session's transcript and links it to the
last commit. Use this when hooks failed to fire or weren't installed when
the session started, or to attach a research session.

If the last commit already has a checkpoint, the session is added to it.
Otherwise a new checkpoint is created.

Use --review to tag the attached session as an agent review. The
first user prompt in the transcript is recorded as the review prompt.
Pass --skills to declare which skills were actually run; omit to
attach a review without a declared skills list.

Works with any registered agent, including external agents enabled via
external_agents in settings. Run 'entire agent list' to see the full list.

If --agent doesn't locate a transcript, Entire auto-detects the agent from
the transcript and prints the detected agent name.

Usage:
  entire attach <session-id> [flags]

Flags:
  -a, --agent string     Agent that created the session (see 'entire agent list' for registered agents, including external) (default "claude-code")
  -f, --force            Skip confirmation and amend the last commit with the checkpoint trailer (best-effort; if the amend fails the checkpoint is still created and the trailer is printed for manual paste)
  -h, --help             help for attach
      --review           Tag the attached session as an agent review
      --skills strings   Optional: declare which review skills were run in this session. Only used with --review
